text:
noah.sales: Heads-up — Orion Health is ready to sign but needs an enterprise commit proposal. Their ask: ~8M tokens/day steady, global peaks up to 200 RPS for ~20m bursts, and ~7k concurrent active chat sessions during core hours. Must include reserved GPU plan, autoscale rules, preheat/runbook, and short, copy-paste answers for security questionnaire. Can we have a draft by Thursday EOD?

anya.solutions: Couple clarifications: which model class do they want as default? Latency SLOs? Are embeddings heavy or occasional? Also any special data residency or fed-region needs?

noah.sales: They prefer an open 13B quantized as baseline for chat, avg 280 tokens per request (prompt+resp), embeddings ~8% of calls. Regions: us-west, eu-west, ap-south. SLO: p95 < 250ms for chat token streaming.

sam.infra: Quick back-of-envelope: 8M tokens/day ~93 tokens/sec average. But bursts drive GPU needs. For quantized 13B on our medium GPUs, assume ~20-25 reqs/sec at ~280 tokens when KV cache warmed. Cold-cache drops throughput ~40%. My proposal: per-region reserved pool of 4 GPUs (hot), plus an ephemeral shared burst pool that can add up to +6 GPUs quickly. That yields steady headroom and handles simultaneous regional spikes.

tess.security: Questionnaire items to prepare: VPC peering & IP allowlist, customer-managed KMS, audit log export (SIEM), data retention settings, SOC2/ISO artifacts. Confirm whether they require HVSM/HSM — that changes timeline.

infra-bot: preheat job scheduled: orion-commit-242512 preheat (KV warm) — est 30m.

anya.solutions: Autoscale suggestion (high level): keep min_reserved=4, max_total=10. Use fast-scale-up route for queue depth and token backlog, but cap per-step to +2 GPUs to avoid noisy neighbor thrash. Add admission policy to shed non-critical long batch jobs during spike windows. Also recommend model-fallback: auto-failover to a smaller quantized 7B variant if queue latency > 400ms for 30s.

sam.infra: Pseudo-config we can hand them (copyable):
```
reserve: 
  per_region: 4
  global_burst_pool: 6
scaling:
  fast_scale_up:
    trigger: token_backlog > 5000 OR avg_request_latency_ms > 150 for 10s
    max_step: 2
    cooldown: 20s
  scale_down:
    trigger: token_backlog == 0 AND avg_cpu < 40% for 90s
    step: 1
    cooldown: 60s
preheat:
  kv_warm_job: enabled
  schedule: 15m before business_window_start per region
fallbacks:
  - condition: queue_latency_p95 > 400ms for 30s
    action: route-new-sessions->model-7B-quantized
    notify: eng-oncall + solutions
```
This enforces short, deterministic scale actions and explicit fallback.

noah.sales: For pricing, they're asking for a commit with a 25% discount target and some burst credits. Can finance/sales model 1yr vs 3yr with burst credits included? Also include how burst credits are consumed (FIFO or proportional).

anya.solutions: Note on cost/throughput: reserved GPUs reduce per-token cost ~22-30% depending on term. Burstable credits effectively smooth peak billing but we should show a worst-case bill when they exhaust burst credits. I'll prepare 12/36mo rows and a simple chart in the doc.

tess.security: On HSM: we can support customer-managed keys via KMS. HSM-backed keys are an enterprise add-on with lead time ~6-8 weeks and requires contract amendment. I'll draft the questionnaire answers marking HSM as optional add-on.

sam.infra: Operational runbook items to hand to the customer:
- Preheat steps (how to run KV warm job, how to validate warm state)
- Autoscale playbook (when to manually bump reserved pool)
- Fallback run instructions (how to flip routing to 7B fallback and back)
- Contact matrix and SLA escalation
I'll sketch a one-page runbook with commands and checks.

infra-bot: monitoring-alert: preheat-job/orion-commit-242512 finished (duration 28m)

anya.solutions: Also recommend canary model rollout pattern: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated quality checks (compare perplexity/response correctness on a small holdout set). That reduces regression risk during model upgrades.

noah.sales: OK action items for Thursday EOD: (1) sam: finalize per-region GPU counts, p95 latency estimates with warm vs cold caches, and runbook draft; (2) anya: 12/36mo pricing with burst-credit burn scenarios + one-pager; (3) tess: questionnaire draft + SOC2/ISO links and HSM note. I'll stitch into a proposal and schedule sign-off call.

sam.infra: Will deliver. Preliminary latency note: with 4 reserved + ability to add 2 GPUs quickly, p95 ~220ms when warmed. Cold-cache p95 could be >500ms unless preheat is run before ramp.

tess.security: I'll attach SOC2 summary and SIEM integration steps. Also will include recommended answers for data residency and retention.

anya.solutions: I'll also include an appendix showing the fallback model quality delta and expected cost delta when falling back to 7B.

noah.sales: Great — thanks everyone. I'll coordinate the customer sync after we have artifacts. If anything changes ping this thread.
